body:
Maintainer decision (2026-11-11): the pin goes to a fork under the owner's account, not to upstream, so the pinned commit cannot disappear.

- Fork: https://github.com/NeoTech/solidcore (fork of `tangency-labs/solidcore`, created 2026-11-11).
- Starting pin: `55d0e7638b9e1ebbf91ab8c10657e595c114ecda` (upstream main at fork time), tagged in the fork as `camcraft-pin-2026-11-11`.
- In `crates/kernel/Cargo.toml` depend with `git = "https://github.com/NeoTech/solidcore", rev = "<full sha>"` for each solidcore crate needed (`solidcore`, `solidcore-step` and what it pulls in). Always `rev`, never a branch or tag name in the manifest.
- Moving the pin later: sync the fork (`gh repo sync NeoTech/solidcore`), pick the commit, tag it `camcraft-pin-<date>` in the fork (a tag keeps it reachable whatever happens to the fork's `main`), then change `rev`. Old pin tags are never deleted or moved.
- Never push CamCraft changes to the fork's `main`; a patch we need goes upstream as a PR, or on a `camcraft/<topic>` branch in the fork, with a decision entry.

If the existing kernel suites do not pass on this commit, pick the nearest one that does, tag it the same way and say so here.

claimed: issue-worker-max (claude-fable-5-2) · 2026-11-11T22:34Z · worktree/branch issue/916-solidcore-step-bench · plan: pin the fork's solidcore workspace at 55d0e763 in crates/kernel with the existing suites green, add a bounded STEP importer on the solidcore side of the seam, bench it against truck-stepio over testdata/models/*.step with a pinned verdict table; tessellation and wasm32 reported as findings.

fix on issue/916-solidcore-step-bench · PR #941 (draft, head 10fabe16) · pinned by step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name, importer_hands_out_closed_forms_and_units, corrupt_step_files_never_panic_or_hang, importer_keeps_its_size_and_time_bounds · merges at the next cut

**The pin.** `55d0e7638b9e1ebbf91ab8c10657e595c114ecda` (tag `camcraft-pin-2026-11-11`) is kept: every kernel suite is green on it, so no nearer commit and no new tag was needed. It is 2973 commits past `solidcore-v1.0.1`. What differed for the seam: `Brep` is no longer `Clone` (test helpers only); the port now refuses a NaN offset; the native reader now refuses blank, foreign, noise and header-only files itself. Five pinned port verdicts re-triaged, all former findings against the port. `Cargo.lock`: 5 git packages replace the 1 registry package.

**Report: where the two importers disagree.**

| File | Unit (mm) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| box.step, empty_list.step (#887), tool_csys_box_iso13399.step | 1 | agree |
| sample_ap214.step (metre, 3 solids) | 1000 | agree |
| Milling-test.step, Milling-test-inch.step | 1 / 25.4 | **disagree: bounding box** |
| tool_csys_none, tool_csys_iso13399, tool_csys_degenerate | 1 | both refuse (the file holds no solid) |

Milling-test is a 60 mm disc with a flat at Y = 19.719. solidcore's volume (52808.744) and area (11143.378) agree with truck's mesh to 1.2e-4, and the inch file reads as the same solid in millimetres. But the port's "tight" bounding box says Y max = 30.0: it takes the whole cylinder, not the trimmed face. The file's vertices, truck's mesh and solidcore's own mesh all stop at 19.719, so solidcore is the wrong side. Filed as #939.

Units agree on all six solid files (1, 25.4, 1000). One difference in kind: the reader alone reads a unit it cannot convert as millimetres without a word, so the seam refuses such a file (as `step_units` does, #306).

**Report: corrupt input.** 19 files made from box.step, each under a 60 s bound that cancels the import: no panic, no hang. solidcore refuses 17 by name and imports the 2 that are whole. truck-stepio, read the way the bench reads it (none of the app's checks after the mesh), refuses the 10 that break the Part 21 syntax and answers `Ok` for the other 9, five of them with an open mesh (a dropped, dangling or unreadable face; a vertex moved 0.5 mm or sent to 1e300). Recorded, not chased: it is about the path the app uses today.

**Report: tessellation (point 4).** solidcore now has a mesher, `solidcore-tess`, which meshes the STEP reader's B-rep record at a chord in millimetres (so the caps of #689 / #864 map onto it directly, with no per-unit conversion). At the app's 0.005 mm chord on the same files:

| | Milling-test.step | sample_ap214.step |
|---|---|---|
| truck: triangles / open sides / volume off exact | 952 / 854 / -1.2e-4 | 3178 / 3196 / -1.5e-4 |
| solidcore-tess: triangles / open sides / volume off exact | 6228 / 0 / -5.6e-5 | 11894 / 0 / -3.1e-5 |

No face left out, none reported over tolerance. Two cautions decide the shape of stage 5: its own docs call it a display mesher, and it reports faces it could not mesh instead of failing; and the bench does not yet measure the largest mesh-to-surface distance. Both are #940.

**wasm32 (point 5).** `cargo check -p camcraft-kernel --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes with the importer in the library.

**Two more findings at the pin** (in #939): the record-to-kernel build leaves a cached face-shell field stale (the seam refreshes it), and the reader's topology pass cannot be cancelled.

**Not done here.** `cargo xtask gate quick` falls back to the batch tier on the `Cargo.lock` change (all of app and ui, and no kernel suite); the kernel suites (25 passed, 2 heavy-lane also passed) and clippy were run instead. The batch tier on this branch is owed before the merge.

Follow-ups: #939, #940 - both gate #917.

PR #941 took `git merge origin/main` (v0.18.0), head ef65c32e, kernel suites green on the merged tree. Correction to the comment above: the pin brings 6 git packages (`solidcore`, `-convert`, `-ops`, `-record`, `-step`, `-tess`; lock 552 -> 557), not 5 - the count was taken before the mesh bench's dev-dependency was added.
